title: The Wow! signal
description: A radio telescope catches something remarkable, and a handwritten Wow! gives it a name. SciShow Space introduces the 1977 detection and the search for a repeat. This 2015 explainer is a starting point, not a current verdict or proof of extraterrestrial contact.
connection: What if a signal really is a message, but you are not its intended listener? Enter the world of numbers stations.

title: Numbers stations: messages hiding in plain hearing
description: Voices read strings of numbers into the shortwave ether. Ringway Manchester explores spy communications and the listeners who document them. The broadcasts are real; an ordinary listener usually cannot identify the recipient or decode the message.
connection: Once you start listening for coded voices, a persistent buzz becomes hard to ignore. What happens when UVB-76 starts talking?

title: UVB-76: voices behind the buzz
description: Ringway Manchester examines voices and sounds associated with the shortwave station nicknamed the Buzzer. Listen for the human activity behind the eerie reputation. Claims that it is a doomsday switch remain speculation, not an established explanation.
connection: Hearing a voice does not settle who controls a signal. In Chicago, someone took over the broadcast itself.

title: The Max Headroom broadcast hijacking
description: Two Chicago television broadcasts were interrupted in 1987 by a masked intruder. The Reyna Bros. documentary examines the footage and the mystery behind it. The intrusion is documented; proposed identities should be treated as theories. Contains crude language and disturbing broadcast footage.
connection: Here we know someone deliberately transmitted. The Wow! signal poses a stranger question: was there a sender at all?
